preconditions.description: The number of test cases T is between 1 and 500 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= N <= 50 for N in [int(lines[i].split()[0]) for i in range(1, len(lines)) if lines[i].strip() and not lines[i].strip().startswith('0') and not lines[i].strip().startswith('1')])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the number of stacks N is between 1 and 50 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(S in ['Dee', 'Dum'] for S in [line.split()[1] for line in lines if line.strip() and not line.strip().startswith('0') and not line.strip().startswith('1')])
preconditions.description: The starting player S is either 'Dee' or 'Dum'.

preconditions.expression: all(all(c in '01' for c in B) and 1 <= len(B) <= 50 for B in [line.strip() for line in lines if line.strip() and line.strip()[0] in '01'])
preconditions.description: Each stack string B contains only '0' and '1' and has length between 1 and 50.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly T lines, one for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(line in ['Dee', 'Dum'] for line in stdout_lines)
postconditions.description: Each output line is either 'Dee' or 'Dum'.

postconditions.expression: all((lambda stacks, starter: (lambda top_vals: (lambda can_move: 'Dee' if (starter == 'Dee' and not can_move) or (starter == 'Dum' and can_move) else 'Dum')(any(v == '0' for v in top_vals) if starter == 'Dee' else any(v == '1' for v in top_vals)))([s[0] for s in stacks]))(stacks, starter) == line for stacks, starter, line in zip(test_cases, starters, stdout_lines))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output correctly identifies the winner based on the game rules: the player who cannot make a move first wins. Specifically, if the starting player has no valid move (no stack with their required top element), they lose immediately; otherwise, the game proceeds optimally, and the winner is determined by the parity of available moves or game state analysis inherent to the optimal play strategy.
